items.title: Chester Zardis Interview, 1970-02-14
items.q: Well, I was waking with, uh, Jack Carey band and, uh, George was with Chris Kelly band.

ctx.x: Uh-huh. Well, tell me about George Lewis at that time. What did, what did he sound like saying that?

George sounded good. George was really, I mean, I didn't know, George just mastered that horn and he had such a wonderful tone, you know? And, uh, everybody admired George's playing. And that's why George got to be known, you know, so much like he did because he had a nice tone and, uh, well, I mean, he was real active. I mean, active. He was great. Because any time, uh, you get on the, uh, I see one time we had a, uh, contest with two bands. Well, I was waking with, uh, Jack Carey band and, uh, George was with…
Yeah. But he, did he play pretty much the same style then? Do you think George was his favorite later when he started to make records?

items.title: Chester Zardis Interview, 1966-03-09
items.q: Sometime I'd be playing at the National Park. And that same old Jack Carey.

ctx.x: You could hear it that far.
Oh yeah. So I just took it for granted. Sometime I'd be playing at the National Park. And that same old Jack Carey.
I was going to ask you about Jack Carey because we have a picture of Punch playing at National Park once.
